title: D115 photographic challenges: history, replies and outcomes
purpose: Preserve each documented return to the photographic argument without losing defenses or manufacturing a score from topical groupings.

coverage.later_episodes: Reconstructed from dated local reports and the live debate ledger, not claimed as recovered verbatim later chat messages.
coverage.episode_selection: Initial critic review and subsequent substantive challenge/reply or measurement episodes; routine status messages are not separate episodes.

counting.reason: Episodes, component rulings and main tally points are distinct units. The number of episode cards is not a score.

photo_subtally.rule: Count only episodes whose recorded outcome is an explicit closed defense or withdrawal. Follow-up tests, component replies, corrections and the unscored F-06 review are excluded.

editorial_history.correction: The earlier 6–0 photo score was constructed by grouping topics after Daniel guessed six. It was not a recovered historical count and is withdrawn. The six topic groups remain an obsolete organizational draft, not a scored result.
Added PH-18, a new available-image measurement check. Episode count is now 18; five explicit closing decisions and existing main tally points remain unchanged.

Added PH-19. Restored a photo subtally on a verifiable rule: explicit closing decisions in this history. Count 6–0 (PH-03, PH-04, PH-07, PH-12, PH-15, PH-19). The earlier 6–0 was a guess and remains withdrawn as such; the new count rests on recorded closing decisions.

episodes.title: Initial critic search
episodes.challenge: Grant, Fodor, Bradley and Ray raised feature-selection, camera, geometry and validation objections.
episodes.daniel_or_author_reply: Daniel asked for the actual critiques and the authors’ replies, rather than treating the existence of criticism as a refutation.
episodes.recorded_outcome: No completed ordinary-solar reconstruction fitting all retained features was found. Several criticisms were meaningful questions; several categorical criticisms misdescribed the method.

episodes.title: Bradley response and actual-method correction
episodes.challenge: Lost depth, changing pixel shadow length, sloping surfaces and allegedly CGI-only validation were presented as challenges.
episodes.daniel_or_author_reply: Daniel supplied Muse’s full response and asked whether Bradley had previously been counted as an effective critic. Muse distinguishes ray correspondences from length measurement and supplies real-photo examples.
episodes.recorded_outcome: These categorical objections were not retained as unanswered defeats. Unknown calibration and feature uncertainty remained questions requiring their own tests.

episodes.title: Mixed sunlight/cloud model: first developed lighting challenge
episodes.challenge: An ordinary 42-degree Sun plus bright overhead fill might create a misleading hat boundary and account for the photographic anomaly.
episodes.daniel_or_author_reply: Daniel insisted the model explain the actual shadows together, the reported dance/descent, and the advance announcement. Dalleur’s reply identifies protected contours missing from the toy rendering.
episodes.recorded_outcome: The model demonstrates a possible selection failure but did not establish that it happened in D115 or supply a better combined explanation. Challenge closed as presented.
episodes.limits: A failed particular model does not exclude every ordinary lighting model; Grant’s scene file was not independently rerun.

episodes.title: Methodology, arithmetic and controls re-audit
episodes.challenge: Do the actual equations, camera sensitivity and validation support the claimed low source, or is there a fatal methodological error?
episodes.daniel_or_author_reply: Daniel requested a full Dalleur/Muse re-audit. Ray-convergence geometry, real controls, historical lens defenses and multiple retained cues answer the categorical criticisms.
episodes.recorded_outcome: Principal result 28.2386 degrees at 37 mm equivalent and intended sensitivity factors reproduce. No fatal methodological error established. Explicit methodology defense retained beneath F-04.
episodes.limits: Reproducing the calculation does not independently authenticate every physical cue or establish a universal one-degree error bar.

episodes.title: Public-image pixel measurement and original-scan issue
episodes.challenge: Could the available image supply an independent check, and does lack of the 6K scan invalidate the published result?
episodes.daniel_or_author_reply: Daniel asked for direct pixel work on the image already available. The original archival scan was sought for better feature selection, rather than made a prerequisite for evaluating the historical case.
episodes.recorded_outcome: Visible boundaries were measured; the conditional two-feature sketch gave about 27.14 degrees. Physical caster/shadow assignments were not independently established. Missing scan access was not counted as evidence of error.
episodes.limits: This is not a second fully independent physical reconstruction or a new defense point.

episodes.title: Camera assumptions: focal length, crop, attitude and shift
episodes.challenge: Could a different focal length, plate/crop, pitch, roll or principal point remove the gap?
episodes.daniel_or_author_reply: Daniel requested an evidence-based audit and then period catalogues, patents and manuals. Muse’s focal-range, face-perspective and thread arguments must be addressed.
episodes.recorded_outcome: Retained-input focal/crop checks did not close the gap. Period shifting fronts were real; centered calibration was not mechanically guaranteed. A mathematical wide/shift candidate required further historical and scene testing.
episodes.limits: Do not turn documented front movement into evidence Ruah used it. Rectilinear wide angle need not show fisheye distortion.

episodes.title: Actual period Protar/camera candidate and explicit withdrawal
episodes.challenge: A Stereoscopic Graphic / 85.7 mm Protar configuration with shifted principal point might reproduce the actual solar elevation.
episodes.daniel_or_author_reply: Daniel pressed for a physically plausible setup and its fit to the whole photograph, especially hanging threads and face perspective.
episodes.recorded_outcome: The candidate could reach the target algebraically but lacked demonstrated mounting and whole-image agreement. The assistant explicitly conceded that its developed physical-camera rebuttal failed.
episodes.limits: This closes the developed candidate, not every possible unusual historical camera.

episodes.title: Hanging-thread measurements
episodes.challenge: Does the proposed setup’s predicted 9–11 degree fringe slant actually fit the shawl strands?
episodes.daniel_or_author_reply: Daniel challenged the visual mismatch and requested direct measurements instead of an assertion of impossibility.
episodes.recorded_outcome: Twelve trace fits had median 4.6 degrees; ten less-sensitive traces had median 5.2. The published calibration was closer on average than that ultra-wide candidate. This supported the existing camera-defense disposition.
episodes.limits: Pixel ridges are not authenticated gravity plumb lines, and neither model exactly matches every trace.

episodes.title: Tangent-based shadow correspondence objection
episodes.challenge: A categorical criticism questioned whether a tangent could provide a valid object-shadow correspondence.
episodes.daniel_or_author_reply: The actual construction was checked against primary computer-vision research. An appropriate common supporting tangent is valid; an arbitrary dark-edge tangent is not.
episodes.recorded_outcome: The categorical tangent criticism was rejected. No contrary set of authenticated D115 feature pairs was established.
episodes.limits: Validity of the supporting-tangent method does not authenticate every historical selected tangent.

episodes.title: Broad-source contact shadows and source identity
episodes.challenge: Granting about 28 degrees, could ordinary extended sky illumination make sharp near-contact edges without being the moving disc witnesses described?
episodes.daniel_or_author_reply: Daniel asked what Muse and Dalleur would say. Their existing defense demands matching all sheltered cues and competing illumination, not merely demonstrating contact hardening in another geometry.
episodes.recorded_outcome: The general optics principle is correct. The illustrative calculation did not supply D115’s actual geometry, cloud radiance or a complete fit; the assistant acknowledged the substantial reply. No new point was awarded then.
episodes.limits: Do not erase the valid contact-shadow principle, or promote it into an established ordinary explanation. This precursor is distinct from the later F-05 decision.

episodes.title: Walkthrough, feature probes and transcript follow-up
episodes.challenge: Does a simplified sharpness objection or an isolated feature inspection engage the actual multi-cue procedure?
episodes.daniel_or_author_reply: Daniel asked to continue with the authors’ explanations and transcripts. The walkthrough shows moving a shared-VP probe across separate features.
episodes.recorded_outcome: The isolated contact-shadow calculation was not a test of the complete procedure. Separate cues supply internal consistency; rays drawn from a shared VP are not automatically independent measurements. No reversal or new challenge point.
episodes.limits: Twenty-one sampled frames were inspected, not a complete independent scene replication. Garment tones do not independently measure drying rate or infrared energy.

episodes.title: A sunlit cloud as both lower light and moving disc
episodes.challenge: Accept the reconstructed lower direction: could a compact sunlit cloud patch also be the reported changing, spinning and plunging disc across observer locations?
episodes.daniel_or_author_reply: Daniel tested the specific cloud drift and motion proposal against D115, witness descriptions and distant reports rather than accepting an unspecified cloud as a complete explanation.
episodes.recorded_outcome: No physically credible joint fit was established. Fixed-height drift conflicts with aspects of the reported motion; changing illumination can evade simple drift tests but no evidenced fitted version was supplied. F-05 explicitly awards Daniel a separate defense.
episodes.limits: Not the same challenge as F-04: here the low direction is granted, rather than explained as a misleading reading. No measured triangulation or exclusion of all atmospheric optics was established.

episodes.title: Geographic localization audit
episodes.challenge: Do published distant-witness lines independently locate a finite source a few kilometres south of the Cova?
episodes.daniel_or_author_reply: The record distinguishes Daniel’s authorization to audit a source claim from adopting that geographic position as a premise. Distant testimony and D115’s direction remain separate evidence.
episodes.recorded_outcome: Independent crossing bearings sufficient for that exact localization were not recovered. F-06 records an unscored correction to a source claim, not defeat of Daniel’s photo case.
episodes.limits: Keep the correction; do not count it as a win against a premise Daniel did not adopt, or erase geographically dispersed reports.

episodes.title: Crowd head directions and the inferred light
episodes.challenge: Can spectators’ apparent viewing directions corroborate the link between the lower illumination and the reported visible object?
episodes.daniel_or_author_reply: Daniel proposed using the heads as additional scene evidence. Six selected faces were fitted under the retained camera model.
episodes.recorded_outcome: Five of six fits broadly point upward/rightward, supporting broad consistency. The fit cannot reliably distinguish 28-degree gaze from about 43 degrees; head pose is not eye direction. Supports existing F-05, no new point.
episodes.limits: Unknown anatomy/pose and indistinct pupils limit precision; shared camera assumptions limit independence.

episodes.title: Joint camera calibration, background trees and Muse’s defense
episodes.challenge: Vary intrinsics, shift and horizon together while preserving the adopted light and vertical vanishing points, producing a solar-elevation solution.
episodes.daniel_or_author_reply: Daniel invoked hanging threads, background trees and Muse’s complementary edge-head and historical-equipment constraints. Preserving one projected vertical family does not answer all those constraints.
episodes.recorded_outcome: The paired-VP ambiguity is mathematically valid, but no historically feasible full scene fit was demonstrated. The recorded F-04 follow-up says this was not sustained as a sufficient objection.
episodes.limits: Trees yielded no independent focal bound. The narrow mathematical degeneracy survives; it is not a demonstrated historical counterexample.

episodes.title: Manuals, measured distortion and propagated ray tests
episodes.challenge: Can period-lens distortion or incorrect historical lens claims bridge the angular gap?
episodes.daniel_or_author_reply: Muse’s differential-endpoint argument was tested against Kinkaid’s original press manual, Magill’s measured lens curves and explicit radial-distortion models.
episodes.recorded_outcome: These checks supported ordinary focal-range practice and small effects in the tested radial models. Corrected the 0.24-percent field-angle citation and a symmetry overstatement; neither supplied a large error or overturned prior defenses.
episodes.limits: The manual is American and from 1936, not a recovered 1917 Ruah inventory. Constructed rays and specimen curves are not calibration of the actual lens or a universal joint-error bound.

episodes.title: Renewed critic review, timing and validation limits
episodes.challenge: Do the current Grant, Ray, Fodor or Bradley arguments, modest timing error, or generic error ranges overturn D115?
episodes.daniel_or_author_reply: The actual method, corrected hat cue, real controls, multi-cue and focal-range replies were retained and checked. A new timing calculation tested modest offsets near noon.
episodes.recorded_outcome: No full ordinary-solar fit or fatal core arithmetic error emerged. Modest timing shifts are too small under the retained model. Feature correspondence and joint uncertainty remain verification tasks, not newly established errors.
episodes.limits: No universal subdegree error distribution, complete independent raw-scan reconstruction or exhaustive global literature absence is claimed.

episodes.title: Raw shadow trace and conditional single-ray plane check
episodes.challenge: Check the real source pixels and correctly identified author cue; determine what a separately measured boundary constrains without inserting Dalleur’s fitted VP.
episodes.daniel_or_author_reply: Daniel requested the shadow check after the five recorded defense decisions. The main crown/brim cue and the demand for valid physical correspondences remain in scope.
episodes.recorded_outcome: Raw edge fitting reproduces 34.1035 degrees within the image. A new single-ray plane test gives a 35.7256-degree maximum at the retained 37 mm camera setting, with all tested unperturbed fit/focal caps below 42.72 degrees. This supports a low direction conditionally. The actual caster/shadow correspondence is not independently authenticated; no full independent source elevation is claimed.
episodes.limits: Same non-blinded image/windows, retained camera assumptions; overlapping fit variants are not independent rays or a confidence distribution. No new tally point.

episodes.title: Lighting conditions at exposure: validation regime challenge
episodes.challenge: Dalleur's real controls are clear-sun scenes where the direct-ray premise holds by construction. D115 was proposed to be dim, hazy or veiled with a bright cloud and sky, so its contact-type cues might be occlusion or diffuse boundaries rather than direct-source rays. A blind test under hazy-sun controls was proposed.
episodes.daniel_or_author_reply: Daniel required testimony substantiating dim or hazy light before reopening the shadows, noted that the pale disc describes the watched object rather than scene illumination, and cited the sharp principal and faint overhead shadows in Dalleur's video.
episodes.recorded_outcome: Garrett (18 December 1917) reports the sun shining clearly and intensely, no fog, light and heat, and clouds that did not dim it. The premise is contradicted; the assistant withdrew the challenge and the proposed CF4 downgrade. Closed defense.
episodes.limits: Does not authenticate every caster and shadow pair or exclude every lighting mechanism. Same family as F-04, so no new main-tally point. The gaze elevation correction is recorded in C12, not scored.
